descriptor: torch 2.7.1 scaled_gemm (m=N, n=M, k=K; A=mat2 transa=T; B=mat1; C=out dtype, fp16 for fp8 outputs; D=out dtype; A/B scale pointers; FAST_ACCUM; MAX_WORKSPACE_BYTES), requestedAlgoCount 1

envelope.K_lookup: B at the smallest grid K >= K
assumptions: 1. at one K and setting, no split far above the largest split M*N seen. The split depends on M and N separately, not on M*N alone, so p1's 24 M values can miss a larger split M*N: p3's dense M found one at 1.12 times the p1 basis (M = 80, N = 2048, K = 8192, the TE fast settings; it enters the bound as raw lo). MARGIN is what covers such an excess. Dense M (p0, p3) exists only at K 1920, 2048, 3584, 4096, 5120, 8192, 11008, 11264, 14336, 18944, 22528 and 28672, with few N; at other K the excess is unmeasured;
2. the split region does not shrink as K grows: a K between grid points takes the next grid K's bound, and every grid K takes the largest bound at or below it;
3. alignment does not matter (p3: no difference between the two alignments of either profile), so the bound has no alignment;
4. the shapes tested: M 1..16,384, N 16..2^20 (p1), model rows to M = 16,384 (p3); a larger M or N is extrapolated in M*N;
5. it holds for this H100 PCIe (114 SMs), driver 570.148.08, cuBLASLt 12.8.3.14, torch 2.7.1's descriptor.
envelope.claim: M * N > B(setting, K) and K_min <= K <= K_max: S = 1
envelope.note: K-dependent bound of the 2026-10-16 split-K sweep (docs/validation_logs/2026-10-16/h100-splitk-sweep): S = 1 for M*N above B(setting, K), K rounded up to the next of 33 grid values, 1,024 <= K <= 4,194,304; sealed held-out test: 1 MiB validated (154,191 held-out shapes above the bound, 0 split); 32 MiB unvalidated (77,518 held-out shapes above the bound, 1 split)

empty_split.what: (S - 1) * ceil(T / S) >= T: a split owns no k-tile

ragged_K.what: K % 128 != 0: the last k-tile is zero padded

split_rule: contiguous: 128-wide k-tiles, split s owns tiles [s*q, (s+1)*q) with q = ceil(T / S); fast one chain per split, slow every tile its own chain added serially from +0; partials added serially; the customOption does not change the result (found after the data came in on the 1,049 live split calls of docs/validation_logs/2026-10-15/h100-probe; the 2,416 live split calls of docs/validation_logs/2026-10-16/h100-splitk-sweep, run after it was fixed, replay equal; 3,465 live split calls in all, customOption 0, 1, 2, 3)

unsplit_customOption_differs.note: keys in both recordings whose unsplit rows (S = 1, same algo / tile / stages / reduction / swizzle) differ in customOption only; the probe's row is kept. cuBLASLt's heuristic gave another customOption for the same key in the sweep's p3 run (its p0 re-run of the probe's grid was identical), so the customOption of an unsplit row is not a function of the key alone

workspace0_note: cuBLASLt never splits without a workspace (0 split rows among the 212,580 workspace-0 queries of the probe, the 653,400 of the sweep's p1 and the 50,000 of its sealed p4; 99,204 table rows)
